clue.text: I'll cut violent male con with tip of potato peeler

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of potato is used
I'll cut means I will cut into the scrambled letters, sitting inside them
violent suggests wild disorder, so the letters of male con are thrown into a new order

parts.note: I'll is I will: the letter I is the one doing the cutting

explanation.surface: A con man is warned that the speaker will attack him with a vegetable peeler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' rearranges MALE CON to OLCEMAN, and 'cut' puts I inside it as OLICEMAN, after P from 'tip of potato'. 'Peeler' is not a kitchen tool here.
explanation.definitionFit: Peelers was an old nickname for officers of the Metropolitan Police, after Sir Robert Peel who founded the force.

clue.text: Sauce quickly runs out

indicators.note: out says the runs are taken away, dropped from the word for quickly

parts.note: presto is the musical direction for very fast, or quickly
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone's sauce is used up in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' and 'quickly runs out' look like one sentence about supplies; 'out' removes R (runs) from PRESTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian basil-and-pine-nut sauce served with pasta.

clue.text: Town council at last has crew working by A-road after phone call

indicators.note: after says the road comes following the phone call in the answer
at last points to the final letter of council

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen
on means working, as a machine that is on
a buzz is informal for a phone call, as in give me a buzz
A plus RD, the standard abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A town council has workers out on a main road after a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: LEIGHTON BUZZARD is a market town in Bedfordshire, England. 'after' places A and RD behind BUZZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Bedfordshire, north-west of Luton, known for its narrow-gauge railway.

clue.text: Name bar opening in Bridport "Speed"

indicators.note: bar means except or exclude, so a letter is left out of the famous person

parts.note: a big name is a famous person, a celebrity

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here the start of Bridport

explanation.surface: A bar named Speed is being opened in the Dorset town of Bridport.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridport is a small town in Dorset. 'bar' means 'except': CELEBRITY loses the B that opens Bridport.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal word for swiftness or quickness of movement.

clue.text: Felt for one spouse needing money abroad

parts.note: a mate is a husband or wife, a partner
the rial is the currency of Iran and other countries, money used abroad

explanation.surface: Someone feels for a husband or wife who needs foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt' reads as a verb of sympathy, but it is the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt is one kind of fabric or cloth, an example of the general term.

clue.text: French article is under par

indicators.note: in a down answer, the article placed under the standard comes after it

parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in up to par
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A French article is below the usual standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French article' looks like LE or UN; here 'French' is the definition and 'article' is the English AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman describes someone or something from Normandy, a region of France, so it can stand for French.

clue.text: Appear happy with daughter's hard work

parts.note: to grin is to look happy
D is the abbreviation for daughter; the 's is a link meaning has

explanation.surface: A parent looks pleased with a daughter's diligent work.
explanation.definitionFit: A grind is laborious, tedious work, like the daily grind.

clue.text: Ploy confines Government at first

indicators.note: at first takes the first letter of Government and puts it at the front

parts.note: ambit is the scope or bounds of something, its confines

explanation.surface: A political ploy keeps the Government boxed in from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confines' looks like a verb, but it is the noun AMBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is an opening move or tactic meant to gain an advantage, a stratagem.

clue.text: One with rather evil bent cast as tyrant

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: cast means moulded into a new shape, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: An actor with a wicked streak is cast as a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges RATHER EVIL BENT to VANTHETERRIBLE, after I for 'One'. The surface reads as theatre casting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV of Russia was a notoriously cruel tsar, the archetypal despot.

clue.text: 1 Across is flawed, having little time for force

indicators.note: for means in place of: the time takes the place of the force

parts.note: defective means faulty or flawed
F is the abbreviation for force in physics
a little time is T, the short form of time

explanation.surface: A policeman is called flawed, with too little time for the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 Across' refers to the answer to 1 across, a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective is a police officer who investigates crimes, a kind of officer.

clue.text: Expert abridged the middle of Peter Pan

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: expert as an adjective means skilled

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter

explanation.surface: An expert has shortened the central section of Peter Pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter Pan' reads as the play, but 'Pan' is the cooking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a frying pan, a heavy cooking vessel with a handle.

clue.text: Farm animal requires long rearing

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
to pant for something is to long for or crave it

explanation.surface: A farm animal needs to stand on its hind legs for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like length, but 'long for' means want, as does PANT.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, a rampant beast is shown rearing up on its hind legs.

clue.text: First to abandon relative, or second

indicators.note: the first letter leaves, so the relative loses its opening letter

parts.note: a mother is a close relative

explanation.surface: Someone asks which comes first in leaving a relative, or perhaps second.
explanation.definitionFit: As in every other day meaning every second day, the word expresses alternation.

clue.text: Forged article is just like the actual thing

indicators.note: forged means hammered into a new shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A counterfeit item is passed off as indistinguishable from the original.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forged' reads as faked, a nice fit with the definition, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A realistic copy is lifelike, true to the genuine original.

clue.text: Split personality perhaps stirred up a riot in Canada

indicators.note: in places the stirred letters inside the abbreviation for Canada

parts.note: CAN is the international code for Canada

indicators.note: stirred up means mixed, so the letters of a riot are jumbled

explanation.surface: A person with a split personality causes a riot in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: Split is a city on Croatia's coast; 'Split personality' is someone from there, not a psychiatric condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is a Croatian city, so a person living in Split is an example of a citizen of Croatia.

clue.text: Give committee a hand finding building material

parts.note: to give a hand is to applaud, to clap
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a round of applause for the committee for finding building supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give committee a hand' puts the applause before the committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapboard is overlapping timber weatherboarding used to clad houses.

clue.text: I half-heartedly look around for cap

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the shortened word is read backwards
half the heart goes: one of the two middle letters is removed

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look

explanation.surface: Someone looks around without enthusiasm for a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one of the two middle letters; 'around' then turns the shortened word round before I.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a French military cap with a flat circular top and a peak.

clue.text: Say, does tackling head off final goal for footballer?

indicators.note: tackling means taking on, so the deer hold the other letters inside

parts.note: does, female deer, are an example of deer, which say signals

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken off the front of final

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A footballer asks whether a tackle that stops the final goal counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' reads as a verb but is the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender is a footballer whose job is to stop the opposition scoring.

clue.text: Fish biting line? They're weighty things to lift

indicators.note: biting means holding in the mouth, so the fish enclose the line

parts.note: barbels are freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Fish taking the bait on a line are heavy to haul out of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbells are long bars with weights at each end used in weightlifting.

clue.text: Decline backing given by a priest

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for decline is reversed

parts.note: to ebb is to decline or fade

explanation.surface: A priest supports a falling-off in something.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is a French abbot or cleric, a priest.

clue.text: Wind's penetrating shelter — it's the talk of the bar!

indicators.note: penetrating means getting inside, so the winds go into the shelter

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
gales are strong winds; the 's makes it plural

explanation.surface: A wind is blowing through a shelter, and it's the gossip of the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but it is the legal profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal jargon is the language of barristers, members of the Bar.

clue.text: Popular entertainer not half showing interest?

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: not half means without half of its letters, the second half going

parts.note: a comedian is an entertainer

explanation.surface: A popular entertainer is said to be not half interesting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' drops the second half of COMEDIAN (DIAN), leaving COME. The question mark flags interest as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest earned on savings is one form of money coming in, earnings.

clue.text: Vague problem producing Chinese food

parts.note: dim means faint or vague
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: An unclear problem results in a Chinese dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum are small Chinese dumplings and snacks served in steamers.

clue.text: Times mag engages worker? That's complicated

parts.note: times as in multiplication, three times four, is three by four

indicators.note: engages means takes on, holding the worker within the magazine

parts.note: a zine is a small magazine
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A magazine called The Times hires a worker, which proves complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but means multiplied BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Byzantine means excessively intricate, from the complex bureaucracy of the Byzantine Empire.

clue.text: Had right tool

parts.note: had as in gave birth to: she bore a child

explanation.surface: Someone owned the correct implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A borer is a tool for drilling holes, such as an auger.

clue.text: Again adjust support around base

indicators.note: around says the support goes round the base

parts.note: a rest is a support, as an armrest
e is the base of natural logarithms in maths

explanation.surface: Someone readjusts a support around its base.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset is to set anew, to readjust or restore a setting.

clue.text: Bewildered, getting less back than one paid

definitions.meaning: confused, not knowing what to do

definitions.text: getting less back than one paid
definitions.meaning: selling something for less than its cost, making a loss

explanation.surface: An investor is confused after receiving less than the outlay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both perplexed and selling for less than cost.

clue.text: French composer considers dropping price

indicators.note: dropping means leaving out, so the price is removed

parts.note: deliberates means considers carefully
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A French composer thinks about cutting his fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Léo Delibes was a 19th-century French composer of the ballet Coppélia and the opera Lakmé.

clue.text: Deposit initially increased tenfold? It's a trick

indicators.note: the first letter, a Roman numeral for fifty, becomes the numeral ten times bigger

parts.note: to lodge is to deposit, as money with a bank

explanation.surface: A savings scheme promising a deposit grows tenfold is a con.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman numerals L is 50 and D is 500, so swapping the first letter L for D multiplies it by ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a cunning trick or scheme to evade something.

clue.text: Disordered situation reflected feeling in market

indicators.note: in places the reversed feeling inside the market

parts.note: a mart is a market

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the word for feeling reads backwards

parts.note: a sense is a feeling, as a sense of loss

explanation.surface: A mood of chaos is mirrored in the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns the feeling backwards before it goes in the market.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare's nest is a muddle or a complicated, confused state of affairs.
